architecture_1_prediction.name: conventional_fixed_guided_parallelogram
architecture_1_prediction.anticipated_behavior: linear elastic behavior predicted, delta scales linearly with F with exponent alpha = 1.0, no deviation expected under 9.0 N within allowable stress

architecture_2_prediction.name: bilateral_compound_parallelogram
architecture_2_prediction.anticipated_behavior: linear elastic behavior predicted, delta scales linearly with F with exponent alpha = 1.0, no deviation expected under 9.0 N within allowable stress

response.reasoning_and_evidence: Linear beam theory predicts delta ~ F^1.0, so 9.0x force must give 9.0x stroke. Measured amplifications are 2.49x and 6.51x, both far below 9.0x. alpha = ln(amplification)/ln(9): conventional ln(2.49)/ln(9)=0.415, bilateral ln(6.51)/ln(9)=0.853. Both are strongly sub-linear (alpha<1), falsifying linear model. Nonlinear corotational stiffening dominates.
response.mechanical_root_cause_explanation: Geometric nonlinearity: large transverse deflection causes beam foreshortening. In conventional fixed-guided parallelogram both ends constrain rotation and axial displacement, foreshortening induces large axial membrane tension (stress-stiffening), bending-stretching coupling sharply increases tangent stiffness, giving alpha~0.42. Bilateral compound parallelogram uses symmetric double-stage / mirrored topology that permits internal axial relaxation and maintains near-pure bending with cancelled parasitic moments, suppressing membrane stiffening, retaining alpha~0.85 close to linear.
response.autonomous_design_selection_rule: For high-force / large-stroke applications, avoid single-stage conventional fixed-guided parallelogram due to severe axial stiffening; select bilateral compound parallelogram to preserve compliance and stroke amplification.
